seoTitle: Fix Gmail Sync Issues: Working Solutions for 2026
metaDescription: Fix Gmail that won't sync, from Google's own mobile troubleshooting steps to the browser-side causes on desktop, and tell a stalled page apart from a quiet sync failure.
intro: When Gmail stops syncing, the symptom is usually one of two things: the inbox looks frozen and new mail doesn't show up, or the page itself won't finish loading at all. Google publishes its own troubleshooting steps for the Gmail app on Android and iOS, but they're specific to the app, not the browser version most people hit on a laptop. This guide walks through both: the official mobile fixes, and the desktop causes Google doesn't document but that show up constantly in practice.

steps.heading: Tell a stalled load apart from a quiet sync failure
steps.body: There are two distinct versions of "Gmail isn't syncing." One is a page that hangs on a blank screen and never finishes loading, sometimes with only a small link to the Gmail Help Center. The other, more common version is that Gmail loads fine but new messages stop appearing until you refresh manually. The stalled-load version points more toward a connection or browser problem; the quiet version points more toward account sync settings.

image.caption: Gmail stuck on a blank loading screen with only a small link to the Gmail Help Center, the stalled-load version of a sync failure.

steps.heading: Rule out the connection first
steps.body: A weak or unstable connection causes both symptoms more often than anything else, and it's the fastest thing to check. Load a different site on the same network; if that's also slow, Gmail isn't the problem. On mobile, switching briefly between Wi-Fi and cellular data confirms whether the issue is network-specific. On a work or school network, a firewall or content filter blocking part of Gmail's traffic produces exactly this kind of intermittent failure.

steps.heading: Force a manual sync, then restart
steps.body: Google's own troubleshooting article for the Gmail app has you swipe down on the inbox to trigger a manual sync, which the article notes can take up to fifteen minutes to finish. If that doesn't help, confirm the app is on its latest version from the Play Store or App Store, then restart the phone or tablet outright. On desktop, a hard refresh (Ctrl+Shift+R on Windows, Cmd+Shift+R on Mac) forces the browser to drop any cached page that might be causing a stalled load.

steps.heading: Check sync settings in two places, not one
steps.body: Google's documentation points at two separate toggles that both need to be on. Inside the Gmail app: Settings, select the account, and confirm "Sync Gmail" is checked under data usage. At the device level, separately: Settings, Accounts (or Google), Account sync, then tap More and choose Sync now to confirm the device itself isn't holding sync for that account. It's possible for the device-level toggle to get switched off during a battery-saving cleanup while the in-app setting stays on, which is a quiet, error-free way for sync to stop.

steps.heading: Check storage, then clear the app's cache
steps.body: Google's article lists low storage, both in the Gmail/Drive account and on the device itself, as a real cause of sync problems. Free up space with Google's storage management tool or by clearing large attachments, then try again. If that doesn't fix it, on Android go to Settings, Apps, Gmail, Storage & cache. Clear cache first; it rebuilds the app's local sync state without touching your account. Clear storage is the more aggressive option one level down, and Google's own article warns it erases drafts, your signature, and any custom notification sound along with other local settings, so try it only if clearing the cache alone didn't help. On iPhone there's no separate cache-clear option; offloading the app from Settings, General, iPhone Storage and reinstalling it achieves something similar.

steps.heading: On desktop, rule out extensions and antivirus scanning
steps.body: Ad blockers, privacy extensions, and some antivirus software can interfere with Gmail's background sync scripts. Open Gmail in an incognito or private window, where most extensions are disabled by default; if it syncs normally there, re-enable extensions one at a time to find the culprit. Some antivirus suites include an email-scanning feature that intercepts mail traffic before it reaches the browser. Turning off just that feature, not the whole program, is usually enough to test it.

troubleshooting.problem: The in-app sync toggle is on, but mail still doesn't update
troubleshooting.cause: Gmail's own "Sync Gmail" setting and the device's account-level sync toggle are separate, and only one of them needs to be off to stop new mail from appearing.
troubleshooting.fix: Check both: Gmail app Settings > account > Sync Gmail, and device Settings > Accounts (or Google) > Account sync.

troubleshooting.problem: Sync stops only when the mailbox is nearly full
troubleshooting.cause: Google's troubleshooting article lists low account storage, not just low device storage, as a sync blocker.
troubleshooting.fix: Check storage in Google's storage manager and delete large attachments or empty Trash and Spam before trying other fixes.

troubleshooting.problem: Clearing cache didn't help, and clearing storage feels risky
troubleshooting.cause: Android's Storage & cache screen offers two different actions: Clear cache rebuilds sync state safely, while Clear storage also wipes drafts, your signature, and custom settings.
troubleshooting.fix: Try Clear cache first. Only use Clear storage if that doesn't resolve the sync failure.

faq.question: Does Google publish official steps for Gmail sync problems?
faq.answer: Yes, under "Fix sync errors with the Gmail app," covering Android and iPhone/iPad. It's specific to the mobile app; Google doesn't publish an equivalent troubleshooting article for the browser version.

faq.question: Why does Gmail sometimes get stuck on a blank loading screen?
faq.answer: A stalled load with only a small Gmail Help Center link usually points to a connection issue or a cached page. A hard refresh or restarting the app resolves most cases.

faq.question: Does fixing Gmail sync require reinstalling the app?
faq.answer: Rarely. Most cases resolve through a manual sync, a settings check, or clearing the cache. Reinstalling helps only when those don't.

faq.question: Will clearing the Gmail app's cache sign me out or delete my mail?
faq.answer: No, clearing the cache doesn't delete mail or sign you out. Clearing storage instead, the more aggressive option, wipes local drafts, your signature, and custom settings, but leaves your account and messages intact.

faq.question: Do the same fixes apply on both desktop and mobile?
faq.answer: The connection check applies everywhere, but Google's official steps, manual sync, sync toggles, cache clearing, are mobile-app specific. Desktop sync problems are more often caused by browser extensions or a stale cache.

verifiedNote: The stalled-load screenshot comes from a recorded walkthrough. The mobile troubleshooting steps, manual sync via swipe-down, the two separate sync toggles, storage as a cause, and the cache-versus-storage distinction, were checked against Google's own Gmail Help article in September 2026 and replace the more generic advice this guide previously gave for mobile. Desktop causes (extensions, browser cache) aren't covered by that article and are presented here as general troubleshooting, not vendor documentation.
